name: Hanor

anatomy.part: left end of the bone bar, where the cord is tied on
right end of the bone bar
knot on the cord, halfway down
crown of the stone, where the cord enters the bob
point of the stone, the tip facing down

myth: When Aun cut the string, the sky went up so fast that his sister Sil had to run after it along the tide. Before he could let go, he had tied a stone to the last of the line, so he would know how far the sky had fallen from the islands. Hesk saw what he had done and kept count of it on her reel. Hanor is that stone. It still swings in the Leeward dark on a line hung from a bar of bone. Each night it hangs a little straighter. The old ones say that when it hangs plumb, the sky will stand up again and come home. Tavo the Gale tries to knock it sideways for sport, and sometimes he does. Then the sailors say the sea has moved under them, and they fall to their knees. Mind your own line, the grandmothers say. Tie a stone to what you fear losing, so you know where it went.
verse:
Hanor swings below,
the stone keeps count of each fall,
plumb, the sky will stand.
